text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P12345 triggered — multiple nodes in cluster `inference-pool-us-east` reporting NotReady and rapid kubelet restarts. Potential customer impact: increased 5xx for hosted inference routes. Link: https://ops.redwood/incident/P12345

oncall-alex: I see the alert. jumping in. any active deployments hitting OOM or CUDA errors in logs?

mira: I noticed spikes in pod restarts on inference replicas 1-3, logs show repeated `kubelet: container runtime error: failed to create task: OCI runtime` followed by `nvidia: driver reset` messages.

sam: running quick node health check now — `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep inference-pool-us-east`

eng-sre-bot: [automated snapshot] Node list: node-q4 (NotReady - Kubelet), node-q7 (NotReady - Kubelet), node-q2 (Ready). Recent evictions: 6 pods evicted from node-q4 in last 5m.

oncall-alex: can we cordon the flapping nodes and drain safe evict the inference pods? want to avoid cache loss but need stability.

tina: agree, cordon -> drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` for affected nodes. also increasing replica count for stable nodes before draining to catch traffic.

mira: proposed commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-q4
kubectl drain node-q4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
kubectl scale deploy/inference-api --replicas=8 -n production
```

sam: running cordon on node-q4 and node-q7 now. starting drain on q4.

oncall-alex: while draining, enable routing fallback to dedicated pool: update routing weight for model-route /v1/generate to prefer dedicated-capacity by 70%. console change posted.

eng-sre-bot: routing policy updated: /v1/generate weight: dedicated=70%, hosted=30% (applied to region us-east).

mira: logs from one restarted pod on node-q4 show: `cuda-driver: GPU reset required` and `oom-kill: task grpc_worker invoked oom-killer`. Looks like mix of GPU driver resets and OOM under heavy batching.

oncall-alex: mitigation checklist: 1) cordon+drain nodes, 2) throttle batching config for productions routes (reduce max_batch_size), 3) scale up stable nodes, 4) trigger cloud provider support for host-level GPU driver flapping. doing 1-3 now.

sam: scaled inference-api to 8 replicas, autoscaler temporarily set to min=6 max=20 to give headroom. throttling batching via runtime config: set `max_batch_tokens` from 4096 -> 2048 for region us-east.

cs-olivia: heads-up: we have two customers with heavy inference traffic in us-east on PLG plan; they might see increased latency or 5xx. I'll prepare a PSAT (short status) to send to CS.

oncall-alex: good. create support page: "Brief: Node flapping in inference-pool-us-east, mitigation in progress — routing fallback and drains applied — potential transient 5xx/latency" and tag customers.

eng-sre-bot: Incident timeline note: 1803456789 alert opened; cordon q4/q7 at 1803456902; drain q4 completed 1803456940; routing fallback applied 1803456955; scale up to 8 replicas completed 1803456990.

mira: after drain, container restarts dropped for pods rescheduled to healthy nodes, but node-q7 continues to show kubelet rapid restarts (systemd shows repeated `kubelet.service` restarts). attaching snippet:```
Apr 12 03:12:42 node-q7 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=137
Apr 12 03:12:43 node-q7 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (kubelet) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

oncall-alex: status: still partial impact, routing fallback holding traffic but we see degraded tail latency. next steps: open cloud provider ticket (NVidia driver flaps + host OOM), collect `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` from affected hosts, and enable ephemeral dedicated fallback for heavy customers.

sam: opened cloud ticket T-9982, included `dmesg` and driver logs. requested escalation to GPU infra team.

mira: quick fix applied — reduced node kube-reserved and system-reserved slightly on kubelet config for this pool to avoid eviction cascades during bursts. also changed `--kubelet-max-pods` not touched. we'll watch for side effects.

oncall-alex: are we planning on a rolling restart of the kubelet on node-q7? need to coordinate with provider ticket.

tina: prefer restart containerd and nvidia drivers after cloud confirms, because kubelet restarts may hide root cause. but if node keeps flapping, schedule rolling reboot of q7 after business hours.

cs-olivia: PSAT drafted and sent to affected accounts. noted mitigation steps and ETA for follow-up. customers acknowledged and asked for update timeline.

eng-sre-bot: note added to incident: Applied routing fallback and scale-up; awaiting cloud provider update. No further 5xx spike after fallback but latency elevated ~200-400ms on tail for 15m.

oncall-alex: handoff planned in 30m to oncall-mira -> oncall-sam for overnight. leaving runbook pointer and actions in incident doc.

mira: leaving detailed checklist in the thread: what to monitor after handoff:
- watch `kubectl get nodes` for NotReady count
- monitor `/metrics` tail latency and 5xx rate for /v1/generate
- monitor GPU driver resets in node dmesg and `nvidia-smi` health
- confirm cloud ticket progress and driver's fix timeline

sam: ack. will monitor, keep routing fallback until 3 consecutive 5m windows with normal error rates.

oncall-alex: final note before handoff: if node flapping persists after cloud action, escalate to infra lead and prepare warm standby capacity in another region as contingency. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident P12345 status updated to "Mitigated (partial)" by oncall-alex.

cs-olivia: posting follow-up to customers with mitigation details and next steps.

mira: leaving logs bundle link in incident doc: https://logs.redwood/incident/P12345/bundle.tar.gz

sam: setting alert suppression on the node flapping rule for 10m while we stabilize to avoid noise.

oncall-alex: handing over to oncall-mira. last check: traffic stable under fallback, will resume full alerting after 10m. handing off. :handshake:

mira: taking over. I have the runbook and will continue monitoring. will escalate if any regression.

eng-sre-bot: Thread closed for handoff.
